statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic zero or greater than 4, the quadratically enriched count of rational plane quartics through eleven general k-rational points is 190H+240⟨1⟩ in GW(k), where H=⟨1⟩+⟨−1⟩.

answer.field: k perfect; characteristic zero or characteristic greater than 4
answer.qualification: All eleven point conditions are k-rational; H=⟨1⟩+⟨−1⟩. The signature is a signed count, not the ordinary number of real curves.

source.location: Setting 1.1; Theorems 1.2 and 1.3; Section 11.1, Table 4, p. 74

scope: General eleven-point configurations and irreducible rational plane quartics.
notes:
The all-rational specialization is repeated in Table 4 from earlier enriched-count work; the 2026 version also treats quadratic extension point constraints.

For the all-k-rational point constraints used here, the underlying enriched correspondence is Jaramillo Puentes–Pauli (arXiv:2309.11706). The later four-author papers explicitly credit that case; their new extension-point results are not needed for this record. Displayed numerical specializations and the rank/signature deduction remain as stated.

Related literature. A quadratically enriched correspondence theorem (Andrés Jaramillo Puentes; Sabrina Pauli, 2023). Historical attribution is retained here. The result’s sole article reference identifies the inspected statement or calculation at the recorded locator.

Source discussion. For eleven general k-rational points, the quadratically enriched count of rational plane quartics is 190H + 240⟨1⟩ in GW(k). Its rank is 620 and its real signature is 240.
